title.abbrev: Strict OTC Verification on RS Sessions

front.title: Strict Only to Customer (OTC) Verification on Route Server Sessions

abstract.t: RFC 9234 requires an AS receiving a route from a lateral Peer to verify that the Only to Customer (OTC) Attribute equals that Peer's AS number, but imposes no equivalent requirement on a Route Server Client (RS-Client) receiving a route from a Route Server (RS). Because an RS is always the apex of any path that traverses it, a route leak that has transited an RS can be accepted without detection.

This document updates RFC 9234 by adding one ingress rule: an RS-Client MUST treat a route received from an RS as a route leak if its OTC value is not the RS's AS number. The check is performed by the RS-Client alone and is therefore effective even when the RS does not implement RFC 9234.

section.name: Introduction
section.t: The OTC Attribute carries an AS number. It is set where a route first ceases to travel "upward" per the Gao-Rexford model (that is, when it is advertised to a Customer, a lateral Peer, or an RS-Client), and is preserved unchanged thereafter. Its value identifies the AS at the apex of the route's propagation path.

Per , a route received from a lateral Peer must carry an OTC value equal to the Peer's AS number or it is a leak (ingress rule 2). No such check exists for a route received from an RS, even though an RS is always the apex of any path that traverses it, exactly as a lateral Peer is. A route arriving from an RS whose OTC value does not match the RS's AS number is a leak and MUST be considered ineligible by the RS-Client.
extends the OTC check on RS-Clients to verify that the OTC value matches the RS's AS number. It is effective against leaks transiting an RS that does not implement .

section.name: Requirements Language
section.t: The key words "MUST", "MUST NOT", "REQUIRED", "SHALL", "SHALL NOT", "SHOULD", "SHOULD NOT", "RECOMMENDED", "NOT RECOMMENDED", "MAY", and "OPTIONAL" in this document are to be interpreted as described in BCP 14 when, and only when, they appear in all capitals, as shown here.

section.name: Terminology
section.t: Terminology follows : the BGP Roles Provider, Customer, RS, RS-Client, and Peer are as defined in its Sections 3.1 and 4, and "local AS" and "remote AS" are the two ends of an eBGP session. "Route is ineligible" is as in . A transparent RS does not insert its own AS number into the AS_PATH of routes it redistributes ; most production route servers are transparent. Example AS numbers are from the documentation range .

section.name: Problem Statement
section.t: checks the OTC value on a route received from a lateral Peer: the value must equal the Peer's AS number, or the route is a leak. It makes no equivalent check on a route received from an RS.

A route server exists to redistribute routes between clients that peer laterally through it. A route that reaches an RS-Client from an RS has therefore just crossed that lateral exchange, and the RS is the highest point on the route's path so far: its apex, in the terms of the Gao-Rexford model and the propagation rules in Section 3.1 of . That is true of transparent and non-transparent route servers alike, since transparency affects only whether the RS appears in the AS_PATH, not its position in the relationship graph.

A route received from an RS must therefore carry either no OTC Attribute or one equal to the RS's AS number. Any other value names a different AS as the apex, which signals a leak has occurred and has been forwarded on by the RS.

shows such a leak. Vertical position reflects the relationship hierarchy, so the RS appears at the apex of the exchange it mediates and the path dips into a valley at AS 64497. The OTC value set by AS 64496 is preserved unchanged all the way to AS 64499.

section.name: Update to the OTC Ingress Procedure
section.t: This section updates Section 5 of . The ingress procedure applying to the processing of the OTC Attribute on route receipt is replaced in its entirety by the following:

ol.li: If a route with the OTC Attribute is received from a Customer or an RS-Client, then it is a route leak and MUST be considered ineligible.

If a route with the OTC Attribute is received from a Peer (i.e., remote AS with a Peer Role) and the Attribute has a value that is not equal to the remote (i.e., Peer's) AS number, then it is a route leak and MUST be considered ineligible.

If a route with the OTC Attribute is received from an RS (i.e., remote AS with an RS Role) and the Attribute has a value that is not equal to the remote (i.e., RS's) AS number, then it is a route leak and MUST be considered ineligible.
If a route is received from a Provider, a Peer, or an RS and the OTC Attribute is not present, then it MUST be added with a value equal to the AS number of the remote AS.

section.t: Rule 3 is new and is the sole normative change made by this document. Rules 1 and 2 are unchanged, rule 4 is rule 3 of renumbered, and the egress procedure is unchanged: an RS-Client continues not to attach an OTC Attribute to routes it advertises to an RS.

The remote AS number used in rules 2, 3, and 4 is the AS number configured for the session. It MUST NOT be inferred from the AS_PATH: a transparent RS does not insert its own AS number into the AS_PATH of routes it redistributes , so the RS's AS number need not appear there at all.

section.name: Backwards Compatibility
section.t: Rule 3 cannot render ineligible any route produced by a deployment in which all participating ASes comply with . Consider the OTC value arriving at an RS-Client over an RS session:

ul.li: If the RS complies, ingress rule 1 has already caused it to discard any route received from an RS-Client bearing an OTC Attribute, so everything it redistributes arrived without one and egress rule 1 attaches the RS's own AS number.
If the RS attaches no OTC Attribute, the route arrives without one and rule 4 attaches the remote AS number, which is the RS's AS number.

section.t: Both cases yield the RS's AS number. Rule 3 can therefore be triggered only by a route whose OTC Attribute was set before it reached the RS, which per requires some AS on the path to have violated the egress procedure. Rule 3 rejects leaks and nothing else.
